policy.acceptable: Optional dependency probes, logging, cleanup, or shell-only formatting paths may keep a broad catch when the fallback is explicit and does not change trust-critical verdicts.
policy.questionable: Active paths that coerce config, pair data, or shape user-visible outputs need a narrower catch or stronger justification before they should remain broad.
policy.should_remove: Trust-critical determinism, guard evidence, guard execution, and pairing logic must not rely on blanket catches because they can hide correctness gaps or downgrade fail-closed behavior.

entries.rationale: Optional adapter-family probing may fall back to None without changing trust-critical verdicts.
Missing package-version metadata is best-effort provenance and is already surfaced as unsupported.
Importlib-resource fallback is a compatibility path and does not decide runtime trust policy by itself.
Error encoding must not fail while packaging an already-raised exception.
Event logging and payload sanitization are best-effort observability paths with explicit fallback behavior.
Inventory hydration is an introspection surface; broad catches only guard optional metadata and plugin-probe failures.
Provider-config itemization is a permissive mapping helper and safely falls back to an empty config.
Plugin discovery and load wrappers are optional-extension surfaces that already reclassify failures into explicit unavailability errors.
The top-level run wrapper catches and records pipeline failures before returning a failed report.
Torch-availability probing is a compatibility path.
These broad catches only protect debug-trace logging and do not change evaluation verdicts.
Emergency rollback attempts are best-effort recovery paths that already preserve failure state in the report.
Latency measurement wraps arbitrary tensor/model calls and immediately re-raises with explicit phase-specific errors.
This catch only protects optional evidence dumping after guard evaluation completes.
Tier-config loading is a compatibility helper that already emits explicit parse errors when strict config content is required.
This catch only protects optional evidence dumping after variance evaluation completes.
CLI bootstrap and top-level dispatch are shell surfaces with explicit fallback behavior.
Backend runtime probing is optional introspection for shell output.
Benchmark command error wrapping is a shell-only concern.
Gate explanation is a read-only reporting shell; these catches affect explanation output, not verdict enforcement.
HTML export is a shell formatting path with explicit nonzero exits.
Plugin listing is an introspection command and the broad catches only protect optional runtime and metadata probes.
Device listing is a probing command and these catches only protect shell diagnostics.
Overhead rendering helpers are shell-only formatting utilities.
Run-artifact shell fallback is best-effort output shaping.
Run-config shell coercion is user-input handling and already degrades to explicit CLI defaults.
Warning-mask rendering is a shell-only display path.
Shell-output formatting should stay best-effort.
Warning filtering is a shell convenience layer and already degrades safely.
